messages:
Oncall-Bot: :rotating_light: Pager surge detected for production inference cluster us-west-2. Primary oncall Sasha marked OOO for holiday. Escalation window in 5m. https://status.redwood.ai/incident/INC-3390001
Sasha: sorry team — got called into family stuff, I flipped my schedule but my phone died. can someone pick up primary for the next 6 hours? :pray:
Mike: I can take primary if needed, currently local and available for the afternoon. will need a quick handoff.
Ana: I can be secondary. I have context on the batching worker that usually trips during lunch traffic spikes.
Sasha: thanks @Mike and @Ana. quick notes: if the KV cache spikes, use the runbook -> "inference-cache-eviction". Link: https://playbooks.redwood.ai/inference-cache-eviction
Mike: ack. Sasha, any recent runbook edits I should be aware of?
Sasha: small tweak last week to the `worker_pool` param. snippet: ```yaml
worker_pool: 16
max_inflight: 128
cache_ttl: 300
```
Sasha: Also, for emergency fallback, switch routing policy to `region-fallback` in the console, that sends a subset of traffic to eu-west until workers stabilize.
Oncall-Bot: Incident INC-3390001 created and pager routed to Mike as primary. Bridge URL: https://meet.redwood.ai/incident/3390001
Mike: joining bridge now. calling out: I'll set myself primary in PagerDuty and start a short blameless triage. anyone monitoring SLO dashboards?
Leo: I'm watching token-latency and error-rate for the affected model route. saw a latency 95th spike to 980ms at t-8m, errors up 0.8%.
Ana: likely cause: KV cache thrash when we had a sudden prefix churn. common pattern: many short requests with different prefixes. runbook recommends increasing cache_ttl temporarily and enabling prefix-level caching.
Mike: ok applying TTL bump to 900s on one pool, will watch. command I ran: ```curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/pools/us-west-2/modify -d '{"cache_ttl":900}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'```
Deploy-Bot: Notified: no active deployments in last 10m. Canary jobs green.
Leo: after TTL bump latency 95th dropped to 420ms within 2m, errors leveling. continuing to monitor.
Ana: if errors persist, failover plan: toggle `region-fallback` for that model route and scale dedicated workers by +2. runbook snippet: ```steps:
  - bump cache_ttl
  - toggle region-fallback
  - scale workers +2
```
Mike: marking oncall note: primary=mike, secondary=ana. I'll own the bridge until 18:30 UTC then hand back to Sasha if they're reachable. adding a short incident summary to the doc.
Sasha: thanks team, appreciate the quick cover. I'm reachable in case phone charges and I can take back if needed. :heart:
Mike: closing bridge in 20m if metrics stay stable. leaving handoff checklist in the incident doc: https://playbooks.redwood.ai/incidents/3390001/notes
Oncall-Bot: Incident INC-3390001 status changed to monitoring. Pager duties updated.
Ana: noted — if you hand back to Sasha, include the TTL change, how long it ran, and the temporary routing change. I'll attach the relevant graphs to the incident.
Mike: final note: customer impact minimal — short tail latency visible to a small subset of APAC requests; no data exposure. adding tags: `coverage-gap`, `holiday-fill`, `kv-cache`.
Sasha: documented. will follow up in morning retro. everyone good to close? :thumbsup:
Leo: :thumbsup:
